subtitle: How Numbers Became the Language of a New Nation

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot against split backdrop of fields and factory chimneys
panels.action: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis stands in profile, one hand on a slide rule, behind him Bengal rice fields fade into rising smokestacks and survey maps.

dialogue.text: In a room in Calcutta, Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis vowed to measure India—its crops, its distances, its dreams—and turned statistics into the language of planning a nation.

i18n.hi: कलकत्ता के एक कमरे में प्रसांत चन्द्र महास्लनोबिस ने कसम खाई—भारत को नापूँगा: खेत, फासले, सपने—और आँकड़ों को बना दूँगा राष्ट्र योजना की ज़ुबान।

panels.shot: slow push-in on contemplative face by a Presidency College window
panels.action: Young Mahalanobis sits at a wooden desk in Presidency College, Calcutta, papers and English journals piled around, gazing out at a busy street of colonial crowds and tramlines.

dialogue.text: In the 1920s, Calcutta’s Presidency College held a restless mind: P.C. Mahalanobis, trained in physics, drawn to numbers, watching a colonial city whose rulers counted imports but not hungry people.

i18n.hi: 1920 के दशक में, कलकत्ता के प्रेसीडेंसी कॉलेज में एक बेचैन दिमाग था: पी.सी. महालनोबिस—भौतिकी में प्रशिक्षित, आँकड़ों की तरफ खिंचा हुआ—देखता एक साम्राज्यिक शहर, जहाँ हुक्मरान आयात गिनते थे, भूख नहीं।

panels.shot: overhead shot of cluttered desk with journals, letters and a map of India
panels.action: Mahalanobis bends over his desk, comparing a British statistical journal, hand-written notes, and a large map of India marked with question marks over vast empty regions.

dialogue.text: Statistics was already a global science. What Mahalanobis saw was its absence in Indian decision-making—no reliable data on crops, villages, or livelihoods, only scattered reports and rough guesses.

i18n.hi: सांख्यिकी दुनिया की विज्ञान बन चुकी थी। महालनोबिस ने देखा कि भारत के फैसलों में उसकी कमी थी—फसल, गाँव, रोज़ी-रोटी पर ठोस आँकड़े नहीं, बस बिखरी रिपोर्टें और अंदाज़े।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot in a small room, friends half-visible as silhouettes
panels.action: In a modest Presidency College room, Mahalanobis stands before a blackboard crowded with symbols, a few young colleagues listening, shelves improvised from bricks and planks behind him.

dialogue.text: On 17 December 1931, in a cramped college room, he founded the Indian Statistical Institute—not as a grand building, but as a resolve: to study numbers rigorously and put them to public use.

i18n.hi: 17 दिसंबर 1931 को, कॉलेज के तंग कमरे में उसने इंडियन स्टैटिस्टिकल इंस्टीट्यूट बनाया—कोई भव्य इमारत नहीं, बल्कि संकल्प: आँकड़ों को सख़्ती से पढ़ना और जनता के काम में लगाना।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of blackboard with multivariate formulas, Mahalanobis gesturing
panels.action: Mahalanobis, sleeves rolled, chalk in hand, stands before equations describing correlations and covariance; students lean forward, the air thick with concentration.

dialogue.text: At the Institute, he wrestled with multivariate data—measurements on many traits at once—and asked a simple, hard question: how do we really measure how far one pattern is from another?

i18n.hi: इंस्टीट्यूट में वह बहु-परिमित आँकड़ों से जूझता रहा—एक साथ कई गुणों की माप—और एक मुश्किल, सीधा सवाल करता: सच में कैसे नापें कि एक पैटर्न दूसरे से कितनी दूर है?

panels.shot: close-up on his hand drawing vectors and ellipses on paper
panels.action: His hand traces points, arrows and an elongated ellipse on a sheet, lines showing clusters and distances not as straight segments, but as paths shaped by the data itself.

dialogue.text: In 1936, in his paper on generalised distance, he introduced what the world now calls the Mahalanobis distance—a way to measure separation that respects the correlations within data.

i18n.hi: 1936 में, सामान्यीकृत दूरी पर अपने पेपर में उसने वो पेश किया जिसे आज दुनिया 'महालनोबिस डिस्टेंस' कहती है—अलगाव नापने का तरीका जो डेटा के भीतर की जोड़ियों का सम्मान करता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a modest ISI office with visitors from different disciplines
panels.action: The ISI room is crowded: economists, botanists, administrators and young mathematicians sit around a table, while Mahalanobis stands at the head, a large ledger open before him.

dialogue.text: From that room grew a hub. Statisticians met economists, agronomists, and civil servants. Mahalanobis insisted that numbers must cross disciplines, because policy lived where science met fields and factories.

i18n.hi: उस कमरे से एक धुरी उभर आई। सांख्यिकीविद अर्थशास्त्रियों, कृषि वैज्ञानिकों और अफ़सरों से मिले। महालनोबिस ने ज़िद की कि आँकड़े दीवारें तोड़ें, क्योंकि नीति वहीं जन्म लेती है जहाँ विज्ञान खेतों और कारख़ानों से मिलती है।

panels.shot: panoramic rural shot with survey team walking through paddy fields
panels.action: Mahalanobis, in simple clothes, walks with a small survey team through Bengal paddy fields, carrying notebooks and measuring rods, farmers watching curiously by the embankment.

dialogue.text: He turned outward to the countryside. Instead of counting every field, he tested large-scale sample surveys—carefully chosen plots whose yields, if designed well, could reveal the harvest of whole regions.

i18n.hi: वह गाँवों की तरफ मुड़ा। हर खेत गिनने की बजाय उसने बड़े पैमाने पर सैंपल सर्वे आज़माए—सावधानी से चुनी ज़मीनें जिनकी पैदावार, ठीक डिज़ाइन पर, पूरे इलाकों की फ़सल दिखा सकती थी।

panels.shot: tight shot of surveyors interviewing a farmer while Mahalanobis observes
panels.action: A surveyor asks a farmer about his crop and land; Mahalanobis stands aside, noting responses, the farmer’s face mixing caution and hope as monsoon clouds gather overhead.

dialogue.text: His 1944 work on large-scale sample surveys showed that, with sound design, a few hundred careful observations could speak for millions, reducing cost without sacrificing honesty.

i18n.hi: 1944 में बड़े पैमाने के सैंपल सर्वे पर उसके काम ने दिखाया कि सही डिज़ाइन के साथ कुछ सौ पक्के अवलोकन लाखों की आवाज़ बन सकते हैं—खर्च घटाकर भी ईमानदारी बचाते हुए।

panels.shot: interior of ISI with young staff tabulating and calculating
panels.action: Inside the Institute, clerks sort punch cards, statisticians compute at desks, wall charts display crop estimates and confidence intervals; Mahalanobis walks between tables, quietly correcting a sheet.

dialogue.text: The Indian Statistical Institute became a workshop of measurement. Crop yields, prices, village surveys—all were processed, checked, and debated before they travelled to the desks of decision-makers.

i18n.hi: इंडियन स्टैटिस्टिकल इंस्टीट्यूट माप का कारख़ाना बन गया। फसलें, दाम, गाँव सर्वे—सब यहीं छँटे, जाँचे और बहस के बाद ही फैसले लेनेवालों की मेज़ तक पहुँचे।

panels.shot: formal mid-shot in Delhi office facing Nehru and officials (figures implied)
panels.action: In a New Delhi office after Independence, Mahalanobis sits across a long table from Indian leaders, charts and projections laid out, the tricolour visible through high windows.

dialogue.text: After 1947, the new Republic needed plans, not just slogans. Mahalanobis moved between Calcutta and New Delhi, bringing his methods to the Planning Commission, arguing that policy must be built on measured realities.

i18n.hi: 1947 के बाद नयी गणराज्य को नारे नहीं, योजनाएँ चाहिए थीं। महालनोबिस कलकत्ता और नयी दिल्ली के बीच चलता रहा, अपनी विधियाँ प्लानिंग कमीशन तक लाकर, दलील देता कि नीति को नापी गई हक़ीक़त पर खड़ा होना होगा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of him pointing to a wall chart of industrial growth projections
panels.action: He stands by a large chart showing projected outputs of steel, machinery and power, fingers marking lines that climb across the decade, officials listening with furrowed brows.

dialogue.text: For the Second Five Year Plan, he advanced a model favouring heavy industry, hoping that investment in steel, power and machines would, over time, lift agriculture and employment through linked growth.

i18n.hi: दूसरी पंचवर्षीय योजना के लिए उसने भारी उद्योग पक्षधर मॉडल दिया, उम्मीद कि स्टील, बिजली और मशीनों में निवेश धीरे-धीरे जुड़ी हुई तरक्की से खेती और रोज़गार दोनों उठाएगा।

panels.shot: split-scene wide: one side a steel plant under construction, other side sparse village
panels.action: On one side, cranes assemble a vast steel plant; on the other, a dry village road with bullock carts and lean figures, the contrast stark under the same sky.

dialogue.text: The plan did raise new plants and capacity, but the record is mixed. Critics later argued that heavy-industry bias slowed agricultural reform and left many villages waiting longer for change.

i18n.hi: योजना से नए कारख़ाने और क्षमता तो उठी, पर नतीजा मिला-जुला रहा। आलोचकों ने बाद में कहा कि भारी उद्योग झुकाव ने खेती सुधार धीमे किए और कई गाँवों को बदलाव के इंतज़ार में छोड़ा।

panels.shot: thoughtful close-up of Mahalanobis reading critical articles at his desk
panels.action: Older now, Mahalanobis sits at his desk, glasses low on his nose, reading a journal article that questions the planning strategy, stacks of survey reports beside him.

dialogue.text: Mahalanobis did not control every outcome. He worked inside political constraints and imperfect data. Later economic histories reassessed his model, but continued to respect his clarity about measurement.

i18n.hi: हर नतीजा उसके हाथ में नहीं था। वह राजनीतिक सीमाओं और अधूरे डेटा के बीच काम करता रहा। बाद की आर्थिक इतिहासों ने उसके मॉडल को फिर से परखा, पर माप पर उसकी साफ़ सोच की इज़्ज़त बनी रही।

panels.shot: wide shot of formal ISI auditorium with him lecturing from a podium
panels.action: In an ISI auditorium, he addresses young statisticians, projection of survey diagrams behind him, audience rows filled with attentive faces from across India.

dialogue.text: “Our duty is simple,” he says. “Measure honestly. Let policy face the facts.”

i18n.hi: "हमारा काम सीधा है," वह कहता है। "ईमानदारी से नापो। नीति को सच का सामना करने दो।"

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot: maps, punch cards, and computer room at ISI
panels.action: A composite scene at ISI: wall maps dotted with sampling points, trays of punch cards, and an early computer room, Mahalanobis walking through, staff collaborating.

dialogue.text: By the time he left the stage, India possessed a statistical system: an Institute, survey methods, and a culture of questioning numbers—not as decoration, but as tools of governance.

i18n.hi: जब तक वह मंच से उतरा, भारत के पास अपना सांख्यिकीय ढांचा था: एक इंस्टीट्यूट, सर्वे की विधियाँ, और आँकड़ों से सवाल करने की संस्कृति—सजावट नहीं, शासन के औज़ार की तरह।

panels.shot: gentle close-up of his face fading into modern scenes of data and planning
panels.action: Mahalanobis’s ageing face, calm and intent, dissolves into a faint overlay of modern satellites, databases, and planners studying maps of India.

dialogue.text: Today we debate growth, inequality, climate and crops using samples, indices and models he helped shape. His legacy is not that plans were perfect, but that he taught a nation to measure before it decided.

i18n.hi: आज हम विकास, असमानता, मौसम और फसलों पर बहस करते हैं उन्हीं सैंपल, सूचकांक और मॉडल से जो उसने सँवारे। उसकी विरासत ये नहीं कि योजनाएँ बेदाग़ थीं, बल्कि ये कि उसने देश को सिखाया: फैसले से पहले नापो।
